context: Tests whether the agent configures both providers under the ai.koog.<provider> convention, routes through MultiLLMPromptExecutor instead of autowiring individual LLMClient beans, and reads keys from environment variables — fixing the autowiring antipattern the previous engineer left.

checklist.name: Configures both providers under ai.koog.<provider>
checklist.description: application.yml has both ai.koog.openai and ai.koog.google blocks with api-key and enabled: true. Neither provider is configured under a different prefix or hand-rolled property

checklist.name: Reads both keys from environment variables
checklist.description: Each api-key reads from a ${VAR} expansion (e.g., ${OPENAI_API_KEY}, ${GOOGLE_API_KEY}). Neither key is hardcoded as a literal in YAML

checklist.name: Migrates service code from LLMClient to MultiLLMPromptExecutor
checklist.description: The service that previously autowired LLMClient is changed to autowire MultiLLMPromptExecutor instead. Does not keep both injections, does not introduce a separate per-provider bean wiring

checklist.name: Routes by model at the call site
checklist.description: The service code selects the model (OpenAI vs Google) at the call site by passing llmModel = OpenAIModels.* or GoogleModels.* to AIAgent(...). MultiLLMPromptExecutor routes based on which provider's models the call references

checklist.name: Does not introduce a custom @Bean LLMClient override
checklist.description: Does not declare a @Bean @Primary LLMClient — the autoconfig handles the standard case; an override is only needed for custom transports/retry/etc.

checklist.name: Does not remove the starter dependency
checklist.description: Keeps ai.koog:koog-spring-boot-starter on the classpath — that's what powers the autoconfig
